survey: The card shows a western saddle sitting on a wooden fence rail. The rail runs left to right under the seat, and its right end meets a vertical post, which is clear in the full card. The seat is a curved leather tub. A horn on a short stem rises at the front (left), and a raised cantle curls up at the back (right). It has a light suede seat panel and stitched edges. A rectangular skirt hangs down the near side, in front of the rail. A second skirt shows behind the rail on the far side, at the right, so the saddle really does straddle the rail and sits on it. A narrow fender or stirrup leather runs down the middle of the near skirt. It ends in a metal buckle, and a wooden stirrup with a tread hangs from that buckle. A second stirrup hangs a little to the right and further back, under the bottom edge of the near skirt. Only a short stub of strap shows above it. The camera looks at the near side from slightly to the front-left and a little above.

errors.where: Second (rear) stirrup, below the bottom edge of the near skirt, right of the front stirrup
errors.what: The far-side stirrup has no clear leather to hang from. It seems to come out from under the near skirt, just behind the front stirrup, rather than from the far skirt behind the rail. So it reads as a second stirrup on the same side, or as a stirrup hanging from nothing, instead of one stirrup on each side of the saddle.

fix: Western saddle sitting on a fence rail. One stirrup hangs on each side of the saddle: the near stirrup hangs from a leather fender on the near skirt, and the far stirrup hangs from its own leather below the far skirt, behind the rail. Show the far stirrup leather clearly connected to the far side of the saddle.
